findings.title: SQL injection via ILIKE search parameter
findings.body: The `index` action interpolates the raw `params[:search]` value directly into a SQL string: `groups.where("name ILIKE ?", "%#{search}%")`. While the `?` placeholder protects against classic injection of the search term itself, the `%` and `_` wildcard characters in the user-supplied search string are not escaped, allowing wildcard injection (e.g. searching `%` matches all groups, `_` matches any single character). More importantly, this pattern is fragile and the change from `ilike` to `ILIKE` suggests a hand-rolled query. The search term should be sanitized (e.g. `search.gsub(/[%_]/, '\\\0')`) or use a proper query builder to prevent wildcard abuse and any future refactoring from introducing true injection.

findings.title: add_members silently ignores usernames with surrounding whitespace
findings.body: In `add_members`, `usernames.split(",")` does not strip whitespace from each username. If the client sends `"user1, user2"` (with a space after the comma, which is common when users type comma-separated lists), `User.find_by_username(" user2")` will return nil and the user will be silently skipped. The member is not added but the response is still `success_json`, so the admin UI shows no error. Each username should be stripped: `usernames.split(",").map(&:strip).each do |username|`.

findings.title: remove_member does not verify the user is actually a member before deleting
findings.body: In `remove_member`, `group.users.delete(user_id)` is called without checking whether the user is actually a member of the group. While `delete` on a non-member is a no-op at the database level, the action still returns `success_json` and calls `group.save`, which triggers unnecessary validations and callbacks. More importantly, if `user_id` refers to a non-existent user, the delete silently succeeds. The controller should verify the user exists and is a member, returning a 404 or 422 if not, so the admin UI can show an appropriate error.

findings.title: add_members and remove_member use params.require(:group_id) but routes define member routes without :group_id segment
findings.body: The routes in `config/routes.rb` define `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` and `put "members" => "groups#add_members"` as member routes on `resources :groups`, which generates URLs like `/admin/groups/:id/members`. However, the controller actions use `params.require(:group_id)`, expecting the parameter to be named `group_id`. With Rails member routes, the id parameter is named `id`, not `group_id`. This means `params.require(:group_id)` will raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` at runtime, breaking both endpoints. The controller should use `params.require(:id)` to match the route definition, or the routes should be defined with an explicit `:group_id` segment.

findings.title: findMembers returns undefined instead of a promise when name is empty
findings.body: The `findMembers` method has `if (Em.isEmpty(this.get('name'))) { return ; }` which returns `undefined` instead of a resolved promise. Previously this returned `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])`. Callers like `setupController` in `admin_group_route.js` (line 13: `model.findMembers()`) and `group-members.js.es6` (line 11: `model.findMembers()`) do not chain on the result, but any future caller that does `.then()` on the result will get a TypeError. More critically, the `removeMember` and `addMembers` methods call `self.findMembers()` in their `.then()` callbacks without returning the promise, which is fine for fire-and-forget, but the inconsistent return type (undefined vs Promise) is a contract violation that can cause subtle bugs.

findings.title: findMembers clamps offset to user_count, preventing access to last page when user_count is not a multiple of limit
findings.body: In `findMembers`, the offset is calculated as `Math.min(this.get("user_count"), Math.max(this.get("offset"), 0))`. This clamps the offset to `user_count`, but the valid maximum offset for pagination is `user_count - limit` (or more precisely, the largest multiple of limit that is less than user_count). For example, if `user_count` is 100 and `limit` is 50, valid offsets are 0 and 50. But if the controller sets `offset` to 100 (e.g., after adding members), this code allows offset=100, which will return an empty page. Conversely, if `user_count` is 75 and `limit` is 50, the second page should be at offset 50, but if someone requests offset 75, it's clamped to 75 which is past the last valid page start. The clamping logic should be `Math.min(Math.max(this.get("offset"), 0), Math.max(0, this.get("user_count") - this.get("limit")))` or the server should handle out-of-range offsets gracefully.

findings.title: Pagination next action can set offset beyond valid range
findings.body: In the `next` action, `offset = Math.min(group.get("offset") + group.get("limit"), group.get("user_count"))`. If `user_count` is 100 and `limit` is 50, and current offset is 50, the next offset becomes `Math.min(100, 100) = 100`. But offset 100 with limit 50 on a 100-user group means the query starts at the 101st user, returning an empty page. The maximum valid offset is `user_count - limit` (i.e., 50 in this case). The `next` action should stop at `user_count - limit` or the `showingLast` computed property should account for this. The `totalPages` computed uses `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` which is also wrong: for 100 users and limit 50, it returns `Math.floor(100/50) + 1 = 3` pages, but there are only 2 pages (offsets 0 and 50). This causes the UI to show "2/3" and allow clicking next to an empty third page.

findings.title: totalPages calculation is off-by-one for exact multiples of limit
findings.body: The `totalPages` computed property uses `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1`. For a group with exactly 100 users and limit 50, this returns `Math.floor(100/50) + 1 = 3`, but there are only 2 pages (offsets 0 and 50). The correct formula is `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`. This causes the pagination UI to show an extra page, and clicking "next" on the last real page navigates to an empty page. The `currentPage` computed has a similar issue with its base calculation.

findings.title: Error handler assumes e.responseText is valid JSON without checking
findings.body: In the `save` action's error callback: `var message = $.parseJSON(e.responseText).errors;`. If the server returns a non-JSON response (e.g., a 500 HTML error page, or a network error where `responseText` is undefined), `$.parseJSON` will throw a SyntaxError, masking the original error and leaving `disableSave` potentially stuck (though `finally` handles that). The code should check that `e.responseText` exists and handle parse failures gracefully, falling back to a generic error message.

findings.title: Stray closing div tag inside table row
findings.body:
Line 19 contains `` inside the `{{#each}}` loop within a `` structure. A `` inside a `` (without a matching opening `
`) is invalid HTML. Browsers will typically ignore it or hoist it out of the table, potentially breaking the table layout. This should be removed.

findings.title: Template iterates over 'members' but controller sets 'model'
findings.body: The template was changed from `{{#each m in model}}` to `{{#each m in members}}`, and the route `group-members.js.es6` now sets `controller.set("model", model)` where `model` is the Group object. The Group model's `findMembers()` sets a `members` property on the group object (line 35 of group.js: `members: result.members.map(...)`). Since the controller is likely an ObjectController or the template context is the group model, `members` should resolve to `model.members`. However, if the controller is not proxying to the model, `members` will be undefined. The template should either use `{{#each m in model.members}}` to be explicit, or the controller should explicitly set `controller.set('members', model.get('members'))` after `findMembers()` resolves. The current code relies on implicit property proxying which may not work depending on the controller type.

findings.title: removeMember action in item view template won't bubble to controller correctly
findings.body: The template `group_member.hbs` uses `{{action "removeMember" member}}` inside an `{{#each member in members itemView="group-member"}}` loop. The `itemView` is `Discourse.View` (from `group-member.js.es6`), not a controller. In Ember, actions in item views bubble to the view's controller, but since this is a plain View (not an ItemView with a specific controller), the action will bubble to the parent controller (the admin-group controller). However, the `removeMember` action expects `member` as a parameter, and in the `{{action}}` helper within an `{{#each}}` with `itemView`, the context may not correctly pass the `member` object. The action should be tested to ensure `member` is correctly passed; alternatively, use `{{action "removeMember" this}}` from within the view's context or use `targetObject` explicitly.

findings.title: members action performs two count queries instead of one
findings.body: The `members` action calls `group.users.count` (line 25) and then `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` (line 26). The `count` query and the subsequent `members` query are separate database queries. While this is acceptable for pagination metadata, the `count` could be optimized by using `group.users.count` only when needed, or by using a single query with `COUNT(*) OVER()` window function (PostgreSQL) to get both total and page in one query. For groups with many members, this is two full queries instead of one. This is a minor performance concern but worth noting for large groups.

findings.title: offset parameter is not validated, allowing negative offsets
findings.body: The `members` action does `offset = params[:offset].to_i` without validating that it's non-negative. A negative offset (e.g., `?offset=-50`) will be passed to ActiveRecord's `.offset()`, which in PostgreSQL treats negative offsets as 0, but this behavior is database-dependent and could cause unexpected results. The offset should be clamped: `offset = [params[:offset].to_i, 0].max`. Similarly, `limit` is not validated to be within a reasonable range (e.g., max 100 or 200), allowing a client to request `?limit=1000000` and potentially cause performance issues.

findings.title: Test for remove_member on automatic group uses wrong HTTP method (PUT instead of DELETE)
findings.body: The test `"cannot remove members from automatic groups"` on line 114-117 uses `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42`, but the route for `remove_member` is defined as `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` in `config/routes.rb` (line 49). The test should use `xhr :delete, :remove_member, ...` to match the actual route. Using PUT will likely result in a routing error (404 or 405) rather than the expected 422, meaning this test is not actually testing the automatic group guard—it's testing that the route doesn't accept PUT. The test passes for the wrong reason.

findings.title: Test for add_members on automatic group uses group_id: 1 which may not be automatic
findings.body: The test `"cannot add members to automatic groups"` uses `group_id: 1`, assuming group with id 1 is automatic. However, group IDs are not guaranteed—the test database may have groups with different IDs, or group 1 may not exist or may not be automatic. The test should explicitly create an automatic group: `group = Fabricate(:group, automatic: true)` and use `group_id: group.id`. Relying on a hardcoded ID of 1 is fragile and may cause the test to pass or fail for the wrong reasons depending on test ordering and database state.

findings.title: Test for remove_member on automatic group uses hardcoded group_id: 1
findings.body: Same issue as the add_members test: the test `"cannot remove members from automatic groups"` uses `group_id: 1` assuming it's an automatic group. This is fragile—the test should create an explicit automatic group with `Fabricate(:group, automatic: true)` and use its ID. Additionally, as noted in the other finding, this test uses `xhr :put` instead of `xhr :delete`, so it's not actually testing the remove_member endpoint.

findings.title: addMembers action has TODO comment indicating incomplete functionality
findings.body: The `addMembers` action contains `// TODO: should clear the input` and does not clear the `usernames` property after successfully adding members. This means after clicking "Add", the user-selector input still contains the previously entered usernames. If the admin clicks "Add" again without changing the input, the same members will be re-added (though the server should handle duplicates gracefully). The `usernames` property should be cleared after a successful add: `self.set('usernames', null)` or `self.set('usernames', '')` in the success callback of `addMembers`.

findings.title: removeMember and addMembers use /admin/groups/:id/members.json but routes expect :id not :group_id
findings.body: The JavaScript model calls `Discourse.ajax('/admin/groups/' + this.get('id') + '/members.json', ...)` for both `removeMember` and `addMembers`. The routes define these as member routes on `resources :groups`, generating `/admin/groups/:id/members`. This URL pattern is correct. However, the controller actions use `params.require(:group_id)` (as noted in the earlier finding about the controller), which expects the parameter to be named `group_id`. With Rails member routes, the parameter is named `id`, not `group_id`. This mismatch means the controller will raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` when these endpoints are called. The controller must use `params.require(:id)` or the routes must be restructured to use `:group_id`.

findings.title: Each loop uses 'members' but controller property may not be set correctly
findings.body: The template uses `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}` but the controller (`admin-group.js.es6`) no longer has a `members` property (it was removed in the diff: `-  members: null,`). The members are now set on the model (the Group object) via `findMembers()`. Since this is an `ObjectController`, `members` in the template should proxy to `model.members`. However, `findMembers()` is async and sets `members` on the model after the AJAX call completes. If the template renders before `findMembers()` resolves, `members` will be undefined. The `setupController` in `admin_group_route.js` calls `model.findMembers()` but doesn't wait for it. The template should handle the loading state, e.g., `{{#if members}}...{{else}}Loading...{{/if}}`.

findings.title: create action does not set alias_level, defaulting to 0 (nobody)
findings.body: The `create` action sets `name` and `visible` but does not set `alias_level`. The Group model likely has a default `alias_level` of 0 (which maps to "nobody" in the UI). This means newly created groups are invisible to everyone by default, which may not be the intended behavior. The admin UI sends `alias_level` in the `save` action (via `asJSON()`), but the `create` action ignores it. The `create` action should also accept and set `alias_level`: `group.alias_level = params[:alias_level].to_i if params[:alias_level].present?`.

findings.title: update action always sets visible even when param is absent
findings.body: The `update` action does `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` unconditionally. If the client sends a PUT request without a `visible` parameter (e.g., only updating `alias_level`), `params[:visible]` is nil, and `nil == "true"` is false, so `visible` is set to false. This means any update that doesn't explicitly include `visible=true` will make the group invisible. The update should only modify `visible` if the parameter is present: `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true" if params.key?(:visible)`.
